source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Document the date and time when the vehicle inspection took place. This should be as accurate as possible to provide a clear timeline of events and to ensure the record is credible.

3. Record the vehicle identification.
Include the vehicle identification number (VIN), make, model, and year. This is crucial to uniquely identify the vehicle in question.

4. Identify the inspector's credentials.
Provide the name and qualifications of the inspector who conducted the brake test, as well as their certification or license number, if applicable.

5. Detail the type of brake test conducted.
Specify whether the test was a hydraulic system check, a dynamic brake test on a roller or inertia dyno, a bleed test, an air brake test for commercial vehicles, or any other specific type.

6. Record the test conditions.
Note the conditions under which the brake test was conducted, including the type of equipment used and any relevant environmental conditions, such as temperature and road surface conditions.

7. Document
